subject: Science
central_question: How do plants make food, exchange gases, transport water and food, and respire to support growth and survival?
in_scope_units: 10.1 How Do Plants Grow?—Activity 10.1 testing the need for water and sunlight.
10.2 How Do Plants Get Food? and 10.2.1 Leaves—Food Factories of Plants, including starch, chlorophyll and Activities 10.2–10.3.
10.2.2 Role of Air in Preparing Food—Activity 10.4 on carbon dioxide and Activity 10.5 on oxygen release.
10.2.3 Photosynthesis—word equation, sunlight, chlorophyll, carbon dioxide, water, glucose, starch and oxygen.
10.2.4 Exchange of Gases in Plants—Activity 10.6 and stomata.
10.3 Transport in Plants—Activity 10.7, movement of water and minerals through xylem, and movement of food through phloem.
10.4 Do Plants Respire?—Activity 10.8 with germinating seeds, lime water and the respiration equation.
In a Nutshell, Let Us Enhance Our Learning Questions 1–10 and exploratory projects.
banned_topics: Detailed chloroplast structure and light-dependent reactions.

known_pitfalls.claim: Plants obtain ready-made food from soil.
known_pitfalls.correction: Plants absorb water and minerals from soil but make food in green parts by photosynthesis.

known_pitfalls.claim: Sunlight and water alone are enough for photosynthesis.
known_pitfalls.correction: Carbon dioxide and chlorophyll are also required.

known_pitfalls.claim: Plants take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide only, even in sunlight.
known_pitfalls.correction: During photosynthesis green parts use carbon dioxide and release oxygen, while respiration continues in plant cells.
Xylem transports water and minerals; phloem transports prepared food.
All living plant parts respire, including roots, stems, leaves and germinating seeds.

recommended_example_progression: Use Activity 10.1 to establish that both water and sunlight support healthy plant growth.
Use Activity 10.2 for the iodine test and Activity 10.3 for chlorophyll and sunlight.
Use Activity 10.4 to demonstrate the requirement of carbon dioxide.
Use Activity 10.5 to identify oxygen released by an illuminated water plant.
Use Activity 10.6 for stomata and Activity 10.7 for xylem transport.
Use Activity 10.8 and Questions 1, 7 and 10 to compare photosynthesis with respiration.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end section 'Let Us Enhance Our Learning' contains Questions 1–10, followed by Exploratory Projects.
